name: Mechanical Sample Preparation
description: Physical preparation of IC and hardware samples for analysis. Covers sample mounting (epoxy potting, vacuum impregnation, clip mounting), cross-sectioning (precision saw, manual cleaving), mechanical polishing (grinding, lapping, final polish to sub-micron finish), and chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP). Includes selection of consumables (abrasives, polishing cloths, mounting resins) and quality verification under optical microscopy.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to mechanical sample preparation

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands sample preparation goals, mounting methods, and polishing stages
evidence: Can explain the purpose of mounting, cross-sectioning, and polishing in the analysis workflow
Understands the difference between rough grinding, fine grinding, and final polishing stages
Aware of how preparation quality affects downstream analysis (optical, SEM, FIB)

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Performs standard mounting and polishing under supervision
evidence: Mounts samples in epoxy resin with correct orientation and minimal void formation
Operates precision saw for cross-sectioning with appropriate blade and feed rate selection
Follows a polishing sequence from coarse to fine abrasives on standard metallographic polisher
Verifies surface quality under optical microscope and identifies common preparation artifacts (scratches, smearing, pullout)

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently prepares samples to target quality for specified analysis goals
evidence: Selects appropriate mounting method (hot/cold mount, clip, vacuum impregnation) based on sample type and target analysis
Achieves consistent sub-micron polish finish suitable for optical layer imaging
Performs CMP to expose specific metal or poly layers at target depth
Documents preparation parameters and maintains preparation logs for traceability

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles difficult samples and unusual geometries; develops preparation recipes; mentors team
evidence: Prepares multi-die stacked packages, interposers, and non-standard geometries
Develops and documents new preparation recipes for novel sample types
Achieves sub-micron planarity and low surface roughness as a basis for FIB-SEM cross-sectioning and ion-milling follow-on preparation
Mentors team on technique selection, artifact prevention, and quality control

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines lab preparation methodology; specifies equipment; trains teams
evidence: Defines the lab's sample preparation SOPs and quality acceptance criteria
Evaluates and specifies polishing systems, consumables, and CMP slurries for procurement
Develops novel preparation techniques for emerging packaging technologies (chiplets, 3D integration)
Conducts proficiency assessments and certification of preparation operators

assessment_methods.description: Prepare a set of samples (cross-section, planview) to specified quality targets, demonstrating correct method selection and finish verification
Review preparation logs and resulting micrographs for quality, artifact control, and documentation completeness

equipment: Precision cut-off saw (e.g., Struers Secotom, Buehler IsoMet)
Metallographic mounting press (hot mount) or cold-mount vacuum impregnation system
Semi-automatic grinding/polishing system (e.g., Struers Tegramin, Buehler AutoMet)
Stereo and compound optical microscopes for quality verification
